All three scenarios pass. I wrote `{"findings": []}` to `openspec/changes/270-rust-inbox-archived/.run/validator/findings.json`. I judged this by reading the code and tests only. As instructed, I ran no build, test or git command.

- **Worktree changes with vcs on and off:** When `vcs.enabled` is set and the project is in git, `read::changes` reads every worktree and stacked folder. Otherwise it reads only the project root. The Landed group now reads only the root's changes. The test `worktree_changes_with_vcs_on_and_off` compares the whole output text both ways: the five Needs you lines with vcs on, and only the `001` line with vcs off. The other groups must be `  (none)` both times. On the base code the inbox read only the root, so the vcs-on check would fail there.
- **Archived worktree changes:** `needs::archived` puts a steering line first when a steering trigger applies (`osq plan`). Otherwise it adds the `archived, not landed — osq land` line, but only when `main` lacks the archive folder and `osq/<folder>` holds an approval. So `004` (no approval) and `007` (merged into `main`) are left out. The test `archived_worktree_changes` builds each row of the table as a real git worktree and checks the full output in order. The base never read worktrees, so this test would fail there too.
- **Config that does not load:** `load_config` errors now become `FeatureError::failed("inbox", …)`. The config loader reads `vcs.enabled` under that exact name, and its errors use the name too. The test `config_that_does_not_load` checks the error kind, the `inbox failed: ` prefix and the `vcs.enabled` text. The base never loaded `osq.toml`, so this case would have succeeded there and the test would fail.

The patch also includes the scope-audit and glob code that came in with the main sync. None of the scenarios cover it, so I didn't judge it.
